tier_note: This is the web tier. It shows results and cannot execute anything. Every capability is listed, including the ones that need the desktop application, with the reason -- hiding one would make this page quietly less honest than the documentation.

operations.label: Check the canonical contract (v1)
operations.description: Re-checks the frozen v1 contract against every rule, its JSON Schema, and its SHA-256 hash chain. Proves the numbers on screen match the file they came from.

operations.label: Check the canonical contract (v2)
operations.description: Same checks for contract v2, which adds the fields the field-data loop produces. v2 is additive: every v1 value survives unchanged.

operations.label: Run the model — canonical (milestone2_v3)
operations.description: Runs the full Python model in canonical mode and regenerates the contract: demand, right-sizing, waits, economics, emissions, confidence and triggers.
operations.unavailable_reason: Running the model executes Python on your machine. The web tier serves precomputed results and cannot execute anything.

operations.label: Run the model — legacy V2 baseline
operations.description: Reproduces the accepted V2 baseline exactly: 25 starter ports, 48 pathway. Kept runnable so the older published figures stay checkable.
operations.unavailable_reason: Running the model executes Python on your machine. The web tier serves precomputed results and cannot execute anything.
operations.caveat: Legacy mode uses the retired 2035/2050 horizons and cohort-relative scoring.

operations.label: Check what field observations would change
operations.description: Reads observed capacity and session records and reports what they WOULD change — which sites upgrade from placeholder capacity, which triggers become evaluable. It never writes: received values enter the inputs and the model re-runs.
operations.unavailable_reason: Reads observation files from your machine. The web tier has no access to your files and cannot run the ingestion.
operations.caveat: No field observations have been received. Today this reports nothing to change, which is the correct answer.

operations.label: Rebuild contract v2 from the frozen v1
operations.description: Widens the frozen v1 contract into v2. Every shared field is copied across unchanged, so 'additive' holds by construction rather than by promise.
operations.unavailable_reason:
Writes files into the repository. The web tier is served as static
                        files and has nowhere to write.

operations.label: Regenerate the static dashboard
operations.description: Rebuilds the nine contract-derived charts, each stamped with the run and source it came from.
operations.unavailable_reason:
Renders and writes image files. The web tier serves the images from
                        the last desktop run instead.

operations.label: Regenerate the Tableau sheet data
operations.description: Rebuilds the seven Tableau sheet tables and the workbook spec from the canonical contract. Publishing to Tableau Public remains a manual, deliberate step.
operations.unavailable_reason:
Writes data files, and publishing drives the Tableau Public desktop
                        application with real keystrokes. Neither is possible in a browser.
operations.caveat: Building the .twbx and publishing need Tableau Public installed and a signed-in session. Four presentation features remain unbuildable — see dashboard/tableau/CAPABILITY_GAP.md.

operations.label: Generate NFC tag payloads and QR fallbacks
operations.description: Produces the NDEF payload for each site tag, a QR code carrying the same URL, and the placement cards. Writing a physical tag is done with a phone.
operations.unavailable_reason:
Writes payload, QR and placement-card files to disk. The web tier
                        offers the already-generated payloads for download instead.

operations.label: Regenerate the workflow documentation
operations.description: Rewrites the workflow step documentation from the executable manifest, so the docs cannot drift from what the code actually does.
operations.unavailable_reason:
Rewrites tracked documentation files in the repository, which a
                        browser cannot do.

operations.label: Review a jurisdiction's own data file
operations.description: Reads a supplied CSV and reports what intake WOULD do with it: which columns it would map and which of those are guesses from a name, which fields are absent, which unit conversions it would apply, and the data confidence the file would produce — all before anything is changed or any run starts.
operations.unavailable_reason: Reads a file from your machine. The web tier has no access to your filesystem, and uploading planning data to a server this project does not run would be a worse answer than not offering the button.
operations.caveat: A proposal, never a run. Nothing is written, no model executes, and the contract is untouched. A mapping guessed from a column name is reported as a guess, and an absent field stays absent rather than being filled with a default.

operations.label: Run every verification gate
operations.description: Runs the whole gate suite — contract rules, hash chains, cross-model constants, published-number checks, secret scan, explorer validity, Tableau and provenance. This is the check CI runs.
operations.unavailable_reason: Executes the full test suite and model runs on your machine. The web tier serves the result of the last CI run instead.
